name: Select Tool
description: Switches to the standard selection tool so clicks and drags pick objects or components instead of transforming them. Reach for it whenever you want to drop out of a manipulator.

name: Move Tool
description: Activates the translate manipulator so you can drag objects or components along axes or planes. The everyday tool for positioning anything in the scene.

name: Rotate Tool
description: Activates the rotate manipulator for spinning objects or components around an axis or the view. Use it with discrete snapping when you need clean angular increments.

name: Scale Tool
description: Activates the scale manipulator for resizing uniformly or per axis. Handy for quick proportional studies before committing to exact dimensions.

name: Show Manipulator Tool
description: Reveals a node's special-purpose manipulator, such as an extrude or projection handle, so you can adjust history inputs interactively in the viewport.

name: Switch to Last Tool
description: Reactivates the most recently used non-default tool, such as a curve or cut tool, without hunting through menus. Useful when alternating between drawing and transforming.

name: Edit Pivot
description: Hold the key (or press Insert) to reposition an object's pivot, then release to lock it in. Essential before rotating doors, arraying panels or mirroring around a specific point.

name: Frame Selected
description: Centres the camera on the current selection so you can work close-up without manually dollying. Press with nothing selected in some panels to frame everything.

name: Frame All
description: Zooms the active view out to fit every visible object, giving you an instant overview of the whole scene or model.

name: Tumble Camera
description: Orbits the camera around its centre of interest by holding Alt and dragging with the left mouse button. The core gesture for inspecting a model from every angle.

name: Track Camera
description: Pans the camera parallel to the view plane with Alt and the middle mouse button. Use it to slide across a facade or plan without changing viewing angle.

name: Dolly Camera
description: Moves the camera towards or away from the subject with Alt and the right mouse button, or via the scroll wheel. Combine with Frame Selected to control zoom precisely.

name: Wireframe Display
description: Shows the active panel in wireframe, exposing topology and hidden geometry at once. Useful for checking edge flow or selecting through objects.

name: Shaded Display
description: Displays smooth-shaded surfaces so you can judge form and massing. The default working mode for most modelling tasks.

name: Textured Display
description: Shows shaded geometry with textures applied, letting you preview materials and UV placement directly in the viewport.

name: Lighted Display
description: Previews the scene using its actual lights instead of default viewport lighting. A quick sanity check on lighting design before rendering.

name: Original Mesh Display
description: Shows the unsmoothed base cage of a polygon mesh. Switch back here when you need to edit raw topology without subdivision preview.

name: Cage and Smooth Preview
description: Displays the subdivided surface with the editable cage overlaid, so you can tweak low-poly control geometry while watching the smoothed result.

name: Smooth Mesh Preview
description: Previews the selected mesh fully subdivided without adding real geometry. Ideal for judging curved forms while keeping the cage light and editable.

name: X-Ray Display
description: Makes shaded geometry semi-transparent via the panel's Shading menu, so you can see and snap to elements behind other objects. Helpful when modelling interiors inside a shell.

name: Wireframe on Shaded
description: Overlays wireframe edges on shaded surfaces from the panel's Shading menu. Great for reading topology density while still seeing form.

name: Isolate Select
description: Temporarily hides everything except the current selection in the active panel. Perfect for detailing one component of a crowded scene without touching visibility layers.

name: Hotbox
description: Holding the spacebar pops up every menu set around the cursor, letting you reach any command without leaving the viewport. A major speed boost once learned.

name: Toggle Panel Layout
description: Tapping the spacebar switches between a single maximised panel and the four-view layout. Use it to jump between perspective work and orthographic checks.

name: Toggle Full-Screen UI
description: Hides or restores all interface panels around the viewport, maximising drawing space on smaller screens or for presentations.

name: Cycle Background Colour
description: Steps the viewport background through dark-to-light greys and the gradient. Switch to a lighter ground when evaluating silhouettes or capturing screenshots.

name: Snap to Grid
description: Hold while dragging to snap the manipulator to grid intersections. Invaluable for laying out geometry on a regular planning module.

name: Snap to Curve
description: Hold while dragging to constrain movement along a curve or edge. Use it to slide setting-out points along a spline or building edge.

name: Snap to Point
description: Hold while dragging to snap exactly onto vertices or CVs. The quickest way to join geometry corner-to-corner with precision.

name: Repeat Last Command
description: Runs the previous command again, such as repeating an extrude or duplicate on a new selection. Saves menu trips during repetitive modelling passes.

name: Marking Menus
description: Holding the right mouse button over an object opens a context marking menu for component modes and common operations. Fast, gesture-driven access to vertices, edges, faces and UVs.

name: Increase Manipulator Size
description: Enlarges the transform manipulator handles for easier grabbing, particularly on high-resolution displays.

name: Decrease Manipulator Size
description: Shrinks the transform manipulator handles when they obscure small geometry you are trying to edit.

name: Toggle Grid
description: Shows or hides the ground-plane grid from the Display menu. Turn it off for clean presentation captures, on for spatial reference and snapping.

name: Poly Count HUD
description: Enables a heads-up display showing vertex, edge, face and triangle counts for the scene and selection. Track it to keep visualisation models within budget.

name: Toggle Object and Component Mode
description: Switches between selecting whole objects and their components such as vertices or faces. The pivot point of the entire polygon editing workflow.

name: Vertex Selection Mode
description: Puts the selection into vertex components so you can pull individual points of a mesh or lattice. Use for fine surface adjustment.

name: Edge Selection Mode
description: Switches selection to edges, ready for bevelling, loop selection or edge sliding. Double-click an edge to grab the whole loop.

name: Face Selection Mode
description: Switches selection to faces for extruding, deleting or assigning materials to specific regions of a mesh.

name: UV Selection Mode
description: Switches selection to UV components, mainly for texture-coordinate work in the UV Editor.

name: Grow Selection
description: Expands the current component selection outwards by one ring of neighbours. Repeat to flood-fill a region quickly.

name: Shrink Selection
description: Contracts the component selection by one ring, trimming the border of a grown selection back down.

name: Soft Selection
description: Toggles soft selection, where edits fall off smoothly across neighbouring components; hold the key and drag to resize the falloff radius. Ideal for organic terrain or fabric-like adjustments.

name: Select All
description: Selects every visible, selectable object in the scene. Useful before scene-wide operations such as grouping or export.

name: Deselect All
description: Clears the current selection entirely. Click empty space or use the menu when precision matters near dense geometry.

name: Invert Selection
description: Swaps selected and unselected objects or components. Handy for hiding everything except your working set or deleting the leftovers of a split.

name: Select Hierarchy
description: Extends the selection to include all children of the chosen nodes. Use before moving or exporting assembled groups so nothing is left behind.

name: Select Edge Loop Tool
description: Selects a continuous loop of edges from one pick; double-clicking an edge does the same. The backbone of clean topology editing.

name: Select Edge Ring Tool
description: Selects the parallel ring of edges running across a loop, useful before connecting or bevelling a whole band of geometry.

name: Select Similar
description: Adds objects or components resembling the current selection, such as faces of similar area. Speeds up bulk edits across repetitive geometry.

name: Pick Walk
description: Steps the selection through the hierarchy or between neighbouring components using the arrow keys: up to parents, down to children.

name: Undo
description: Reverses the last action; press repeatedly to step back through history (Z alone also works). Raise the undo queue limit in Preferences for heavy modelling sessions.

name: Redo
description: Reapplies an action you just undid (Shift+Z also works). Use alongside Undo to compare before-and-after states of an edit.

name: Delete
description: Removes the selected objects or components from the scene. Deleting edges this way leaves stray vertices behind; use Delete Edge/Vertex for clean removal.

name: New Scene
description: Starts a fresh, empty scene, prompting you to save unsaved changes first.

name: Open Scene
description: Opens an existing Maya scene file, replacing the current one.

name: Save Scene
description: Saves the current scene to its file. Save often; combine with Increment and Save to keep dated versions of design stages.

name: Save Scene As
description: Saves the scene under a new name or location, useful for branching a design option without touching the original file.

name: Increment and Save
description: Saves a copy with an automatically incremented version number. A lightweight versioning habit that protects design iterations.

name: Import
description: Brings the contents of another file, such as an OBJ, FBX or Maya scene, into the current scene. Use for merging consultant models or asset libraries.

name: Export Selection
description: Writes only the selected objects out to a new file in a chosen format. The standard route for handing individual assets to other software.

name: Create Reference
description: Links an external scene into the current one without merging it, so the source file can keep evolving independently. Use for shared site models or repeated building assets.

name: Optimize Scene Size
description: Cleans unused nodes, empty transforms and stale data from the scene to reduce file size and improve stability. Run it before archiving or sharing files.

name: Attribute Editor
description: Toggles the panel showing every attribute of the selected node across its full node network. Go here when the Channel Box's summary is not enough.

name: Channel Box
description: Shows the keyable transform and shape channels of the selection for quick numeric entry; Ctrl+A toggles between it and the Attribute Editor. Type exact values here for precise placement.

name: Outliner
description: Opens the hierarchical list of everything in the scene for selecting, renaming, parenting and reordering. The primary window for keeping a complex model organised.

name: Node Editor
description: Opens a graph view of node connections for building and debugging shading networks, constraints and procedural setups. More technical than the Attribute Editor but far clearer for complex networks.

name: Script Editor
description: Opens the MEL and Python console where every action is echoed as a command. Copy echoed commands from here to build shelf buttons and automate repetitive tasks.

name: Hotkey Editor
description: Lets you inspect and remap every keyboard shortcut in Maya. Visit it to bind frequent tools like Multi-Cut to spare keys.

name: Preferences
description: Opens Maya's settings, including working units, up axis, undo queue and viewport options. Set units to metres or millimetres before starting architectural work.

name: Polygon Cube
description: Creates a primitive box, the usual starting block for massing studies and hard-surface modelling. Adjust subdivisions in the Channel Box before editing.

name: Polygon Sphere
description: Creates a primitive UV sphere with adjustable axis and height subdivisions. A base for domes, light fittings and organic forms.

name: Polygon Cylinder
description: Creates a primitive cylinder, useful for columns, handrails and circulation cores. Set cap and side subdivisions before deforming.

name: Polygon Plane
description: Creates a flat, subdividable plane, the common start for terrain, floor plates and facade panels.

name: Polygon Torus
description: Creates a ring-shaped primitive with controllable section radius. Useful for curved balustrades, ring beams and abstract forms.

name: Type
description: Generates editable 3D text as extruded, bevelled polygon geometry with live attributes for font, tracking and depth. Handy for signage and titles in visualisations.

name: Combine
description: Merges several polygon objects into a single mesh so their components can be edited and welded together. Combine before merging vertices or bridging between parts.

name: Separate
description: Splits a combined mesh back into independent objects along its disconnected shells. Use after Boolean or Combine operations to regain individual parts.

name: Fill Hole
description: Caps an open border of a mesh with a single face. Quick fix for gaps left by deleted faces before smoothing or Boolean work.

name: Reduce
description: Decimates a mesh to a target percentage or triangle count while trying to preserve shape. Use to lighten scanned site meshes or heavy consultant models.

name: Remesh
description: Rebuilds a mesh with evenly sized triangles, improving the base for sculpting or further retopology. Useful on messy imported geometry.

name: Retopologize
description: Automatically rebuilds a mesh with clean, mostly quad topology. A fast route from scan or sculpt data to geometry you can actually edit.

name: Smooth
description: Subdivides the mesh for real, rounding forms and multiplying face counts. Prefer Smooth Mesh Preview while designing and apply Smooth only when needed.

name: Triangulate
description: Converts every face to triangles, guaranteeing planar geometry for export to game engines or analysis tools.

name: Quadrangulate
description: Merges triangles back into quads where possible, making imported triangulated meshes friendlier to edit.

name: Mirror
description: Duplicates the mesh across a chosen axis and can merge the seam vertices automatically. The standard finish for symmetrical models built as one half.

name: Boolean Union
description: Fuses two meshes into one solid volume, removing the internal geometry. Useful for welding massing volumes together, though clean topology is not guaranteed.

name: Boolean Difference
description: Subtracts one mesh from another, ideal for cutting window and door openings out of walls. Expect to tidy the resulting topology afterwards.

name: Boolean Intersection
description: Keeps only the overlapping volume of two meshes. Useful for finding shared volumes or trimming a form to a site envelope.

name: Cleanup
description: Finds and optionally fixes problem geometry: nonmanifold edges, lamina faces, zero-area faces and more. Run it before Booleans, smoothing or export.

name: Transfer Attributes
description: Copies vertex positions, UVs or normals from one mesh to another with matching or similar topology. A rescue tool when UVs were made on an earlier version of a model.

name: Extrude
description: Pushes selected faces, edges or vertices outwards to create new connected geometry, with thickness, divisions and optional curve guidance. The single most-used modelling command, from raising walls to panelling facades.

name: Bevel
description: Rounds or chamfers selected edges with controllable width and segments. Essential for catching light on otherwise razor-sharp architectural edges.

name: Bridge
description: Builds connecting faces between two border edge runs on the same mesh, with optional divisions and curvature. Use for linking towers, looping handrails or closing gaps.

name: Circularize
description: Rearranges selected components into a perfect circle, ideal for preparing a flat region to receive a cylindrical extrusion such as a rooflight.

name: Collapse
description: Collapses selected edges or faces so each shrinks to a single point, removing detail while keeping the surface closed. Useful for simplifying topology locally.

name: Connect
description: Inserts new edges linking selected components, splitting the faces between them. A precise alternative to Insert Edge Loop when you only need a partial connection.

name: Detach
description: Splits selected components apart so faces no longer share vertices, letting you peel geometry open. Use before pulling a panel away from a surface.

name: Merge
description: Welds selected vertices that fall within a distance threshold into single points. The standard way to stitch combined meshes together seamlessly.

name: Merge to Center
description: Welds all selected vertices into one point at their average position. Quick for closing a fan of edges at a pole or apex.

name: Average Vertices
description: Relaxes selected vertices towards the average of their neighbours, smoothing lumps without adding geometry. Apply repeatedly for a gentle ironing effect.

name: Chamfer Vertex
description: Replaces a vertex with a small flat face, cutting the corner. Useful for detailing junctions or preparing corner geometry.

name: Delete Edge/Vertex
description: Deletes selected edges together with their now-redundant vertices, keeping the mesh clean. Always prefer this over plain Delete for removing edges.

name: Extract
description: Detaches the selected faces into a separate shell or object, leaving a hole behind. Use to break a facade panel or roof plane out of a massing model.

name: Poke
description: Adds a vertex at the centre of each selected face and fans edges to its corners. Handy for creating apex points for pyramidal roofs or spikes.

name: Wedge
description: Extrudes faces along an arc around a selected edge, sweeping out a wedge shape. Useful for curved ramps, vault segments and pipe elbows.

name: Add Divisions
description: Subdivides selected faces or edges a set number of times without changing shape. Use when a region needs more resolution for detailing or deformation.

name: Edit Edge Flow
description: Repositions selected edges to follow the surrounding surface curvature, keeping inserted loops from flattening a curved form.

name: Symmetrize
description: Copies geometry from one side of a topological symmetry axis to the other, restoring symmetry after asymmetric edits.

name: Append to Polygon Tool
description: Builds new faces by clicking around open border edges, filling gaps with controlled topology. More precise than Fill Hole when the shape of the patch matters.

name: Create Polygon Tool
description: Draws a new polygon face point by point on the grid or in space. Useful for tracing site boundaries or floor outlines before extruding.

name: Crease Tool
description: Assigns crease weights to edges so they stay sharp under smooth mesh preview or smoothing. Lets you keep crisp architectural arrises on subdivided models without extra edge loops.

name: Insert Edge Loop
description: Slices a continuous loop of edges around a mesh with one click, adding resolution exactly where you need it. Fundamental for controlling curvature and adding structural lines.

name: Multi-Cut
description: Cuts new edges anywhere on a mesh: click-drag freeform cuts, slice along a plane, or insert loops with snapping. The Swiss-army knife for custom topology.

name: Offset Edge Loop
description: Inserts two new edge loops equally spaced either side of a selected loop. Quick way to frame a band of faces for panelling or glazing bars.

name: Quad Draw
description: Draws clean quad topology directly on a live reference surface, point by point. The core manual retopology tool for rebuilding scans or sculpted forms.

name: Slide Edge Tool
description: Slides selected edges or loops along the surrounding surface without breaking the surface shape. Use to fine-tune loop placement after insertion.

name: Target Weld Tool
description: Drag one vertex or edge onto another to weld them together interactively. The tidy way to close small gaps and merge corners one at a time.

name: Sculpting Tools
description: A brush-based toolkit for pushing, smoothing, grabbing and relaxing mesh surfaces. Well suited to shaping terrain models and organic freeform studies.

name: Soften Edge
description: Sets selected edges to shade smoothly, blending normals across them. Use on curved surfaces so facets disappear without adding geometry.

name: Harden Edge
description: Sets selected edges to shade with a crisp break, ideal for keeping architectural edges reading sharply under smooth shading.

name: Reverse Normals
description: Flips the facing direction of selected faces so they render and shade correctly. Fix inside-out geometry from imports or mirrored copies.

name: CV Curve Tool
description: Draws a NURBS curve by placing control vertices that pull the curve towards them, giving the smoothest results. The standard start for rails, profiles and setting-out lines.

name: EP Curve Tool
description: Draws a NURBS curve that passes exactly through each point you click. Prefer it when tracing survey points or a plan underlay precisely.

name: Bezier Curve Tool
description: Draws curves with familiar Bezier anchor-and-handle control, similar to Illustrator's pen. Comfortable for designers coming from 2D vector tools.

name: Three Point Circular Arc
description: Creates an exact circular arc through three placed points. Useful for setting out curved walls and bays from known geometry.

name: NURBS Circle
description: Creates a NURBS circle, a versatile profile for sweeping handrails, columns and extrusions along paths.

name: NURBS Sphere
description: Creates a NURBS sphere primitive with editable surface degree and spans. Useful when downstream surfacing operations need true curvature.

name: NURBS Plane
description: Creates a flat NURBS surface patch with adjustable spans, a base for trims, projections and surface modelling exercises.

name: Loft
description: Skins a smooth surface through an ordered series of profile curves. The classic way to build hulls, canopies and freeform roofs from sections.

name: Planar
description: Fills a closed, flat curve (or curves) with a trimmed planar surface. Quick for floor plates, glazing panels and any flat infill.

name: Revolve
description: Spins a profile curve around an axis to create a surface of revolution. Ideal for domes, columns, balusters and vessels.

name: Birail
description: Sweeps one or more profile curves along two rail curves, giving precise control of both edges of the resulting surface. Excellent for gridshell-like roofs and complex transitions.

name: Extrude (NURBS)
description: Sweeps a profile curve along a path curve or straight direction to form a surface. The NURBS route to handrails, mouldings and extruded sections.

name: Boundary
description: Builds a surface spanning three or four boundary curves. Useful for patching openings between existing surface edges.

name: Attach Surfaces
description: Joins two NURBS surfaces into one, blending or keeping their shapes at the seam. Use to consolidate patchwork surfacing into cleaner spans.

name: Detach Surfaces
description: Splits a NURBS surface into separate pieces along chosen isoparms. The surface equivalent of cutting a panel line.

name: Insert Isoparms
description: Adds isoparms to a NURBS surface, increasing local control without changing its shape. Do this before detaching or sculpting a region.

name: Offset Surface
description: Creates a parallel copy of a surface at a set distance, like offsetting a wall face to create thickness. Pair with Loft between edges to close the solid.

name: Rebuild Surfaces
description: Reconstructs a surface with a specified number of spans and degree, evening out parameterisation. Essential housekeeping before further surfacing operations.

name: Reverse Surface Direction
description: Flips a surface's U, V or normal direction. Fixes surfaces that shade dark or trim the wrong way after mirroring or importing.

name: Trim Tool
description: Removes regions of a surface inside or outside curves-on-surface, like cutting openings in a curtain wall panel. Requires the surface to carry projected or intersected curves first.

name: Untrim
description: Restores a trimmed surface to its full untrimmed extent, undoing previous trims without losing the underlying surface definition.

name: Project Curve on Surface
description: Projects a curve onto a surface along a view or vector, creating a curve-on-surface ready for trimming or as a construction line. Use it to map plan geometry onto sloping or curved forms.

name: Intersect Surfaces
description: Creates curves where two surfaces cross each other, ready for trimming either side. The set-out for junctions between intersecting roof or wall surfaces.

name: Surface Fillet
description: Builds a smooth blend surface between two surfaces, such as a circular fillet along their junction. Use for coved junctions and smooth transitions between shells.

name: Attach Curves
description: Joins two curves into a single curve, blending or connecting at the ends. Use to consolidate traced segments into one clean rail.

name: Detach Curves
description: Splits a curve into separate curves at selected points or curve parameters. Use to isolate the span you need for a loft or sweep.

name: Fillet Curves
description: Creates a rounded corner between two curves, optionally trimming them back. The drafting-style fillet for plan geometry.

name: Cut Curve
description: Cuts curves where they cross each other, discarding or keeping segments. Tidies intersecting setting-out lines into clean segments.

name: Intersect Curves
description: Creates locator points where curves intersect, useful reference for snapping or measuring set-out geometry.

name: Insert Knot
description: Adds an edit point to a curve without changing its shape, giving extra local control exactly where you need it.

name: Extend Curve
description: Lengthens a curve beyond its end by distance or to a point, keeping continuity. Use to run a rail past its surface before trimming back.

name: Offset Curve
description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance, exactly like a drafting offset. The basis for wall thicknesses, kerbs and repeated contours.

name: Rebuild Curve
description: Reconstructs a curve with a chosen number of spans and uniform parameterisation. Rebuild scruffy traced curves before lofting for far cleaner surfaces.

name: Duplicate Surface Curves
description: Extracts isoparms, edges or curves-on-surface as independent curves. The way to harvest a surface's edge to drive the next loft or sweep.

name: Group
description: Gathers the selected objects under a new transform node so they move, hide and duplicate as one. The basic building block of a tidy scene hierarchy.

name: Ungroup
description: Removes a group node and returns its children to the parent above. Use when a temporary grouping has served its purpose.

name: Parent
description: Makes the selected objects children of the last-selected object, so they follow its transforms. Fundamental for assemblies such as door leaves on frames.

name: Unparent
description: Detaches the selected objects from their parent, moving them to world level while keeping their position.

name: Duplicate
description: Creates a copy of the selection in place, ready to move into position. Everyday duplication for repeated elements.

name: Duplicate with Transform
description: Repeats the last duplicate along with the transform you applied to it, so move-and-press again builds an evenly spaced run. Perfect for fence posts, mullions and stair treads.

name: Duplicate Special
description: Duplicates with options: instances instead of copies, numeric offsets, mirrored scales and multiple counts. The dialog to reach for radial arrays and instanced facade modules.

name: Delete History
description: Removes the construction history stacked behind the selected objects, baking their current shape. Do this once a model is final to lighten the scene and prevent history glitches.

name: Delete Non-Deformer History
description: Deletes modelling history while preserving deformers such as skins and blend shapes. The safe history clean-up on rigged or deforming models.

name: Hide Selection
description: Hides the selected objects from view without deleting them. Clear the decks around whatever you are focusing on.

name: Show Last Hidden
description: Reveals the objects you most recently hid, the quick undo for an over-eager Hide Selection.

name: Show All
description: Makes every hidden object visible again. Run it before final checks so nothing is accidentally left out of a render or export.

name: Center Pivot
description: Moves an object's pivot to the centre of its bounding box. The first fix when rotation or scaling behaves oddly on imported geometry.

name: Freeze Transformations
description: Zeroes the selection's translate and rotate values and sets scale to one while keeping it in place. Freeze before rigging, arraying or exporting so transforms read cleanly.

name: Reset Transformations
description: Returns the object to the origin by zeroing its transform values. Useful for snapping strays back to a known datum.

name: Match Transformations
description: Copies another object's position, rotation, scale or pivot onto the selection. Align replacement components exactly where their predecessors sat.

name: Align Objects
description: Lines up selected objects by their bounding-box edges or centres along chosen axes, like align tools in 2D layout software. Quick tidy-up for rows of furniture or panels.

name: Snap Together Tool
description: Click a point on one object and a point on another to snap the first into contact, with optional rotation to match surfaces. Handy for assembling kit-of-parts models.

name: Make Live
description: Turns a surface into a live construction surface that new curves and Quad Draw strokes stick to. Essential for drawing accurately on terrain or scan meshes.

name: Search and Replace Names
description: Renames many objects at once by substring, prefix or suffix. Keep naming conventions intact across imported or duplicated geometry.

name: Add Attribute
description: Adds a custom attribute to the selected node, such as a flag or dimension you want to track and key. Foundation for simple custom controls and metadata.

name: Create Display Layer
description: Creates a layer from the selection so groups of objects can be hidden, templated or made unselectable together. Maya's equivalent of drawing layers for managing consultant models and design options.

name: Quick Select Set
description: Saves the current selection as a named set you can reselect instantly from the Edit menu or Outliner. Ideal for recurring selections like all glazing faces.

name: Create Set
description: Creates an object set that membership-tracks its contents for lighting, rendering or export groupings. More formal than quick select sets and usable by other tools.

name: UV Editor
description: Opens the 2D editor where texture coordinates are laid out, cut, sewn and arranged. Home base for preparing models for materials, decals and texture baking.

name: Planar Mapping
description: Projects UVs onto the selection from a single flat plane. Best for flat elements like walls and floors; expect stretching on anything curved.

name: Cylindrical Mapping
description: Wraps UVs around the selection as if projected from a cylinder. Suits columns, drums and curved wall segments.

name: Spherical Mapping
description: Projects UVs from a surrounding sphere, appropriate for domes and globe-like objects.

name: Automatic Mapping
description: Projects UVs from several directions at once and lays the pieces out without overlaps. A fast, serviceable starting point for complex or blocky geometry.

name: Cut UV Edges
description: Splits UVs along the selected edges, defining seams where a shell will open out. Place seams where they will be least visible on the finished material.

name: Sew UV Edges
description: Joins UV shells back together along selected shared edges, removing unwanted seams.

name: 3D Cut and Sew UV Tool
description: Lets you drag along mesh edges in the viewport to cut or sew UV seams interactively, like tailoring directly on the model. The most intuitive way to plan seams.

name: Unfold
description: Relaxes UV shells so they flatten with minimal stretching, like pressing a pattern flat. Run after cutting seams to get even texture distribution.

name: Optimize UVs
description: Iteratively relaxes UVs to reduce local distortion after unfolding, without moving shell boundaries dramatically.

name: Layout UVs
description: Packs all UV shells neatly into the 0-1 texture square with even spacing and optional scaling. The final tidy before texturing or baking.

name: UV Snapshot
description: Exports an image of the UV layout to paint over in image software. The bridge between Maya's UVs and hand-authored textures.

name: Set Key
description: Records a keyframe on all keyable channels of the selection at the current time. The fundamental act of animating anything, from a sun study to a walkthrough camera.

name: Set Key on Translate
description: Keys only the translate channels of the selection, keeping rotation and scale untouched. Cleaner curves when only position is animated.

name: Set Key on Rotate
description: Keys only the rotate channels of the selection, useful when animating a turntable or an opening door leaf.

name: Set Key on Scale
description: Keys only the scale channels of the selection, for growth diagrams or phased massing animations.

name: Play/Stop Playback
description: Starts or stops timeline playback in the viewport. Your constant companion when reviewing animation timing.

name: Go to Start of Playback
description: Jumps the current time back to the start of the playback range, ready to replay from the top.

name: Next Frame
description: Steps the current time forward one frame for frame-by-frame review of motion.

name: Previous Frame
description: Steps the current time back one frame.

name: Next Key
description: Jumps the time slider forward to the selection's next keyframe, ideal for hopping between poses.

name: Previous Key
description: Jumps the time slider back to the previous keyframe of the selection.

name: Auto Keyframe
description: Toggles automatic keying so any change to an already-keyed channel records a new keyframe. Speeds up blocking but switch it off when tweaking static scenes.

name: Graph Editor
description: Opens the curve view of animation, where keys and tangents shape motion over time. Where you refine an ease-in on a camera move or fix a wobble.

name: Dope Sheet
description: Opens a spreadsheet-like view of keys against time for retiming many objects at once. Better than the Graph Editor for shifting blocks of timing.

name: Time Editor
description: Opens a nonlinear editor for arranging animation clips on tracks, like video editing for motion. Use it to sequence and blend reusable animation clips.

name: Playblast
description: Captures viewport playback to a movie file for fast, un-rendered animation review. The everyday way to check camera moves and timing before committing to renders.

name: Set Driven Key
description: Links one attribute to drive another, such as a slider rotating a whole array of louvres. The no-code way to build parametric-style relationships.

name: Bake Simulation
description: Converts constrained, driven or simulated motion into plain keyframes on every frame. Bake before exporting animation to engines or other packages.

name: Editable Motion Trail
description: Displays an object's path over time as an editable curve in the viewport, with keys you can drag in space. Excellent for smoothing camera paths through a building.

name: Ghost Selected
description: Shows faded copies of an object at surrounding frames so you can judge motion spacing at a glance, like onion-skinning in 2D animation.

name: Euler Filter
description: Fixes rotation curves that flip through unnecessary 360-degree spins by re-expressing them continuously. Apply when imported or constrained rotations suddenly whirl.

name: Create Joints
description: Places a chain of joints by clicking, forming the skeleton that will drive deforming geometry. The starting point of any rig, from a character to an articulated canopy.

name: Insert Joint
description: Adds a new joint into an existing chain, splitting a bone into two. Use when a rig needs an extra articulation point.

name: Mirror Joints
description: Duplicates a joint chain across a chosen plane with correct naming and orientation. Build one arm or leg and mirror the other.

name: Orient Joint
description: Aligns joint local axes consistently down the chain so rotations behave predictably. Run before binding; badly oriented joints haunt a rig forever.

name: Create IK Handle
description: Adds an inverse-kinematics handle so a chain bends automatically to reach a goal, rather than rotating each joint by hand. Standard for legs, pistons and struts.

name: Bind Skin
description: Attaches a mesh to a skeleton so joints deform it with weighted influence. The step that turns geometry plus joints into an animatable figure.

name: Unbind Skin
description: Detaches a mesh from its skeleton, optionally keeping the current deformed shape. Use when rebinding after skeleton changes.

name: Paint Skin Weights
description: Opens a brush interface for painting how strongly each joint influences the mesh. Where most skinning time is spent smoothing deformation around joints.

name: Mirror Skin Weights
description: Copies painted skin weights from one side of a symmetrical mesh to the other, halving the painting workload.

name: Copy Skin Weights
description: Transfers skin weights between meshes, such as from a proxy onto the final model. Saves repainting after topology changes.

name: Blend Shape
description: Morphs a mesh between sculpted target shapes with weighted sliders. Used for facial animation and equally handy for blending between design variants of the same form.

name: Shape Editor
description: Opens the editor for creating and organising blend shape targets and their weights, with in-between and combination shapes.

name: Lattice
description: Surrounds geometry with a cage of control points; moving the cage smoothly deforms everything inside. A quick way to taper, bulge or bend a whole massing model.

name: Cluster
description: Binds a set of points to a single handle with adjustable weights, so one control moves a weighted region. Useful for tweaking curve CVs or localised surface adjustments.

name: Delta Mush
description: Smooths deformation artefacts while preserving surface detail, cleaning up rough skinning or lattice results with one deformer.

name: Wire Deformer
description: Deforms a surface using one or more curves as handles, like bending a sheet with drafting splines. Intuitive for curving canopies and fabric-like surfaces.

name: Nonlinear Bend
description: Applies a controllable bend deformer along an axis of the selection; siblings include twist, taper, flare, sine and wave. Excellent for curving straight geometry such as arcing a bridge deck.

name: Parent Constraint
description: Makes an object follow another's position and rotation without changing the hierarchy, with animatable weights. The rigger's way to have a camera or prop hand over between targets.

name: Point Constraint
description: Pins an object's position to one or more targets, averaging by weight, while leaving its rotation free.

name: Orient Constraint
description: Matches an object's rotation to one or more targets without moving it. Useful for keeping arrayed elements facing a common direction.

name: Aim Constraint
description: Keeps an object pointed at a target, like heliostat panels tracking the sun or a camera locked to a focal point.

name: Scale Constraint
description: Ties an object's scale to one or more targets, keeping proportional relationships across linked elements.

name: Pole Vector Constraint
description: Controls which way an IK chain's knee or elbow points by aiming its bend plane at a target object. Standard finishing touch on limb rigs.

name: Hypershade
description: Opens the material editor where shading networks are built by wiring texture and utility nodes together. The hub for creating and organising every material in the scene.

name: Assign New Material
description: Creates a material and applies it to the selection in one step, via the right-click marking menu or Hypershade. The fastest route from grey model to first material pass.

name: Standard Surface
description: Maya's physically based all-purpose material covering metals, glass, plastics and architectural finishes through layered parameters. Start here for almost any realistic surface (Arnold's equivalent is aiStandardSurface).

name: Directional Light
description: Creates a light with parallel rays like the sun, the workhorse for daylight studies and exterior shots. Rotate it to set time of day; position does not matter.

name: Point Light
description: Creates an omnidirectional light radiating from a single point, useful for bare bulbs and quick fills.

name: Spot Light
description: Creates a cone-shaped light with adjustable angle and falloff, suited to downlights, wall-washers and stage-like accents.

name: Area Light
description: Creates a light that emits from a rectangular surface, giving soft, realistic shadows. The go-to for luminous ceilings, windows and softboxes in interior renders.

name: Arnold SkyDome Light
description: Creates a dome light that wraps the scene in an HDRI environment, providing realistic sky illumination and reflections in one node. Usually the first light in an architectural visualisation.

name: Arnold RenderView
description: Opens Arnold's interactive renderer, which updates progressively as you adjust lights, materials and cameras. Your live feedback loop while developing an image.

name: Render Settings
description: Opens the settings for renderer choice, resolution, sampling quality and output paths. Configure here before rendering stills or sequences.

name: Render Sequence
description: Renders the full frame range of the current camera to image files from within the interface. Suitable for shorter sequences when a farm or batch setup is overkill.

name: Light Editor
description: Opens a spreadsheet-style overview of every light in the scene for soloing, muting and adjusting intensities side by side. Invaluable when balancing complex interior lighting.

name: Create Camera
description: Adds a camera object you can place, aim and animate, then look through for composed views. Create dedicated cameras for each key view rather than moving the perspective view.

name: Look Through Selected
description: Switches the active panel to look through the selected camera or light via the Panels menu. Essential for composing shots and aiming spotlights precisely.

name: Create nCloth
description: Turns a mesh into simulated cloth that drapes, folds and collides within the nucleus solver. Useful for fabric canopies, curtains and tensile structure studies.

name: Create Passive Collider
description: Makes a mesh act as a solid obstacle that cloth and particles collide against without being simulated itself. Set floors and frames as colliders before draping fabric over them.

name: Create Emitter
description: Creates an nParticle emitter that sprays particles into the scene for effects such as fountains, rain or crowd-flow experiments.

name: MASH Network
description: Creates a procedural network that scatters and arrays instanced geometry with distribution, random and signal nodes. A parametric-style tool for facade modules, repeated furniture and generative studies.
